characters: Vivian: a 15-year-old girl in a JHS 3 uniform, with a pile of untouched notes and a worried face.
Reuben and Mercy: her study-group friends, 15, with flash cards and a flask of water.
Mr Ampadu: the form master, in a grey shirt, writing a timetable on the board.
The classroom: a JHS 3 room with a revision timetable and a countdown calendar on the wall.

narrationPlan.voice: Lively students; a calm, practical voice for Mr Ampadu
narrationPlan.pace: Quick and funny at the panic, calm and steady at the plan (about 125 words per minute)
notes: Read dialogue with a different voice for each character.
Pause for two seconds at each question activity.
Never rush the last page: let the ending land.

music: Ticking clock and quick strings at the panic; a calm, steady tune at the plan (placeholder)
culturalNotes: The students, teacher and school are invented. Mock exams are a common practice before the BECE in Ghanaian schools.
The study methods (timetables, flash cards, mind maps, past questions, sleep) are widely recommended; teachers should adapt them to local needs.
The letter on page 7 is exam-safe: full words, correct spelling and linking words that organise ideas.
reviewQuestions: Is the language right for the stated age band and reading level?
Is anything here inaccurate, stereotyped or unsafe for children?
Check the claim that sleep helps memory against a reliable education or health source before use in class.
Check that the study advice (forty-minute sessions, phone away) is presented as suggestions, not rules.
Check the letter format against the BECE marking scheme.

teacherGuide.overview: A story about preparing for mock exams with a plan, a study group, healthy habits and calm. It models an advice letter in exam-safe English.
learningGoals: Write an advice letter using linking words.
beforeReading: Ask: what is your biggest challenge when preparing for an exam?
whileReading: At page 2, ask learners to start their own timetable.
afterReading: Write a letter to a younger cousin with four pieces of study advice.
Create a personal revision timetable for one week.
discussion: Why does studying with friends help?
What are the risks of cramming?
reflection: Which study habit will you start this week?

mathsExtension.task: A learner studies 40 minutes a day for 6 days. How many hours and minutes?
An exam is 90 minutes long and has 6 questions. About how many minutes per question if 15 minutes are kept for checking?

support: Provide a timetable template with days, subjects and break times.
stretch: Make a poster “Mock Week Survival Guide” with five tips and reasons.

culturalNotes: The students, teacher and school are invented. Mock exams are a common practice before the BECE in Ghanaian schools.
The study methods (timetables, flash cards, mind maps, past questions, sleep) are widely recommended; teachers should adapt them to local needs.
The letter on page 7 is exam-safe: full words, correct spelling and linking words that organise ideas.
localiseThis: Match the subjects and exam dates to your school’s calendar. Include learners with no home study space by offering school study time.
